record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.context_brief: relaxation gap for r=1 independent set
record.original_question: For a continuous graph Γ, let α_1(Γ) be the maximum size of a 1-independent set in Γ, and let α(G(Γ)) be the size of a maximum independent set in the associated combinatorial graph G(Γ) on the same endpoints. The paper asks whether the ratio α_1(Γ(G)) / α(G) is always at most n/2 for an n-vertex graph, whether that bound is tight, and more generally how this ratio behaves for special graph classes and structural restrictions.

evidence.quote: It is unclear whether or not n/2 is a tight upper bound for the ratio α1(Γ(G))/α(G). We leave this as an open question of this section. Furthermore, we do expect that some structural properties of combinatorial graphs influence the ratio, and it is interesting to see how the ratio behaves in special cases/classes of graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A continuous graph is a pair Γ = (V, E) where V is a (possibly infinite) set of points in a metric space and E is a set of continuous curves (edges), each curve having two endpoints in V; distinct edges may share interior points. Given a finite simple graph G = (V(G), E(G)) on n vertices, a continuous realization of G is any continuous graph Γ(G) whose endpoint set is V(G) and whose edge set realizes E(G) by continuous curves in the plane (or in some ambient space).

For a continuous graph Γ, a subset S of points of Γ (vertices together with possibly interior points of edges) is called 1-independent if no two points of S lie on a common edge (i.e., on the same curve) of Γ. Let α_1(Γ) denote the supremum of |S| over all 1-independent sets S in Γ. For a finite simple graph G, let α(G) denote the usual independence number, i.e., the maximum size of a vertex subset of G containing no edge.

Problem. For every finite simple graph G on n vertices and every continuous realization Γ(G) of G, is the inequality
    α_1(Γ(G)) / α(G) ≤ n/2
always valid? If yes, is this bound tight, and which graphs (or classes of graphs) attain it? More generally, determine how the ratio α_1(Γ(G)) / α(G) behaves under structural restrictions on G (for example, sparsity, bounded degree, planarity, bipartiteness, or chordality), and identify the extremal classes.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. The question is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on combinatorial properties of continuous graphs, and a web search returns no follow-up work establishing tightness of the n/2 bound on the ratio α_1(Γ(G))/α(G) or characterizing its behavior for special graph classes.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs (survey listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey explicitly leaves the tightness of the n/2 bound for α_1(Γ(G))/α(G) as an open question and asks how the ratio behaves on special graph classes.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as open in the most recent survey on continuous graphs.
